  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:

      required:

          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1

        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits; the result must have 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. The E.164 string (e.g. '+61412345678') is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. The effective date must fall on a business day: if it lands on
            a Saturday or Sunday it is rolled forward to the following Monday, and
            that adjusted date is what is stored and returned.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2013-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only opt-in flag for create. When true it allows creating an
            owner that shares a household (same lastName and address, compared
            case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) with an existing owner;
            otherwise such a create is rejected 409. Not persisted or returned.
          type: boolean

          default: false
          example: false

        - type: object

              readOnly: true

              description: >-

                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'
                where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of city,
                LAST3 the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN
                is a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned on create
                (one more than the number of owners already in that city).
              type: string
              example: 'SYD-SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for owners who live in the same
                household (same lastName and address, compared case-insensitively
                with collapsed whitespace). Assigned on create when the request
                sets sharesHousehold true: all owners sharing the household

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:

            membershipLevel:

              type: integer

              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3

            locality:

## What I changed

Consolidated the three separate duplicate checks (telephone, email, household) into a single derived **`identityKey`** = `normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + householdId`, rejecting a create with **409** only when a new owner's *whole* key matches an existing owner's.

**New files**
- `OwnerIdentity.java` — the single definition of the key. The telephone component is normalized to E.164 (reusing `OwnerTelephones`), email is lower-cased (empty when absent), householdId is used as-is (empty when not in a shared household).
- `EnsureUniqueOwnerIdentity.java` — the one dedup step: computes the new owner's key and compares it against every existing owner's key.
- `DuplicateIdentityException` + handler + escalation YAML — responds 409 with `field: identityKey`.

**Pipeline (`owners.POST.yml`)**
- Removed the `ensureUniqueTelephone` / `ensureUniqueEmail` / `ensureUniqueHousehold` steps.
- Added `ensureUniqueIdentity` **after `assignHousehold`**, so the householdId component of the key is already assigned before the comparison runs. `NormalizeOwnerTelephone` (the 400-on-invalid step) is untouched.

**Response**
- Added the readOnly `identityKey` field to the `Owner` schema in `openapi.yml` and derived it in `OwnerMapper` via a `toIdentityKey(owner)` expression, so every owner response now returns `identityKey`.

**Cleanup**
- Deleted the three old `EnsureUnique*` functions, their `Duplicate*` exceptions/handlers and escalation YAMLs, and fixed the now-dangling `{@link}` references in `OwnerTelephones`, `OwnerHousehold`, and `AssignOwnerHousehold`.

**Behavioural effect (as specified):** because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same `householdId`) with different telephones now have different `identityKey`s and are both allowed — only an exact full-key match is a duplicate. The acceptance test `coreRejectsIdentityCollision` (same telephone → same key → 409) passes.
